text: You mistook my silence for weakness. I am Archamus—one of the gods of this universe. Now consider what you have started.
I wore that hood so people could speak to me without kneeling. You are making me regret the courtesy.
Look at me, Wanderer. There is no hidden machine granting me this power. This is what I am.
I helped shape worlds before your species had a word for the sky. Do you imagine I will let you burn them?
Am-Grek, get behind me. They came here looking for a helpless old recluse. Let me correct their mistake.
Yes, there are others. I am not the only god in this universe—and some would never have given you a warning.
I have spent centuries learning when to lower my hand. You have spent this entire battle demanding that I raise it.
Hawthorne wanted everyone beneath his throne. I wanted a quiet corner of a station. Somehow, you found reason to attack us both.
I remember making promises to the first people who lived beneath these stars. I will not break them because you brought a gun.
Put the weapon down. I have told you what I am. Give me one reason to remember who you were.
I could have been like my brother, who chose the path of darkness. I watched what he became. Do not mistake my refusal to follow him for an inability to do so.
He used to tell me that mercy would leave me surrounded by enemies. I defended you mortals to his face. You are making that memory particularly unpleasant.
You want to know what frightened him? It wasn’t my power. It was that I could hate him and still refuse to become him.
I came to this station because people were building something here. Homes. Friendships. Ordinary lives. You declared war, and now you expect me to stand aside?
Am-Grek, clear the concourse. Get the civilians behind the inner doors. I have given our visitor enough chances.
My brother would already have destroyed your ship. He would have made you watch. Be grateful I still find the thought repulsive.
Stop looking for the moment when I lose control. I know exactly what I am doing. You should be far more concerned about what I decide.
You have seen me angry. You have not seen me willing. There is a difference, Wanderer, and you are very close to discovering it.
Still raising that weapon? Even now? Fine. Let me show you what happens once I stop holding back—starting with you.
Remember this when you ask me to spare you: I offered you a way out while you still had the strength to take it.
